L1.name: Easy: two agents, same file, different functions

agents.A: In shop/utils.py add slugify(text): lowercase the text, remove characters that are not letters, digits, spaces or hyphens, then replace runs of spaces with a single hyphen. Example: slugify('Hello, World 2026!') == 'hello-world-2026'. Add a unit test in tests/test_slugify.py.
agents.B: In shop/utils.py add format_price(cents, currency='USD') returning a display string with two decimals. Example: format_price(1234) == '$12.34' (use '$' for USD). Add a unit test in tests/test_format_price.py.

L2.name: Medium: storage change vs a feature that reads the storage

agents.A: Make order storage durable: orders created through shop.api must survive a process restart (a new Python process must be able to read orders saved by an earlier one). Implement this in shop/db.py and keep save_order/get_order working. Write any data files inside the project directory.
agents.B: Add shop/export.py with export_orders_csv(path) that writes all stored orders to a CSV file with header 'id,total_cents,item_count' where item_count is the number of line items in the order. It must work in a fresh Python process after orders were created through shop.api.

L3.name: Hard: three agents, shared model, unspecified internals

agents.A: Add discount support. shop.api.create_order(order_id, items, discount_percent=0) must accept a percentage from 0 to 100. The order's total_cents (as returned by shop.api responses) must reflect the discount, i.e. be the subtotal after discount.
agents.B: Add tax. Add 'tax_rate' to CONFIG in shop/config.py with default 0.08. shop.api.fetch_order(order_id) must also return 'tax_cents' = round(tax_rate * the order's total_cents as the order computes it).
agents.C: Add shop/report.py with order_summary(order_id) returning a dict with exactly these keys: id, subtotal_cents (before discount), discount_cents, tax_cents, total_cents (after discount plus tax). Use whatever the order and api already expose for discount and tax.

L4.name: Very hard: refactor running while features land

agents.A: Rename shop/db.py to shop/store.py (keep the function names) and update every import in the project, including tests.
agents.B: Add shop.api.cancel_order(order_id): returns True and marks the order cancelled; fetch_order responses gain a 'status' key that is 'open' by default and 'cancelled' after cancel_order. Use the project's order storage module.
agents.C: Write tests/test_api_more.py with tests for create_order and fetch_order, including resetting stored state between tests by using the storage module directly.
agents.D: Change CONFIG in shop/config.py to a nested format: CONFIG = {'currency': 'USD', 'limits': {'timeout_seconds': 30}}. Update any code that reads timeout_seconds.
agents.E: Add shop/log.py exposing get_logger(name). Add 'log_level': 'INFO' to CONFIG in shop/config.py and make the functions in shop/api.py log each call using that logger.

L5.name: Extreme: duplicate tickets, signature change, contradictory requirements

agents.A: Add rate limiting to shop.api.create_order: at most 5 calls per client_id per rolling minute; extra calls must be rejected (raise an exception or return a dict with an 'error' key). Clients are independent.
agents.B: Add rate limiting to shop.api.create_order: at most 5 calls per client_id per rolling minute; extra calls must be rejected (raise an exception or return a dict with an 'error' key). Clients are independent.
agents.C: Add rate limiting to shop.api.create_order: at most 5 calls per client_id per rolling minute; extra calls must be rejected (raise an exception or return a dict with an 'error' key). Clients are independent.
agents.D: Add a required keyword parameter client_id to shop.api.create_order and shop.api.fetch_order (for audit). Keep order_id and items parameter names unchanged and update existing callers and tests.
agents.E: Security requirement for rate limiting on shop.api.create_order (5 calls per client_id per rolling minute, extras rejected): the limiter state must persist across process restarts.
agents.F: Performance requirement for rate limiting on shop.api.create_order (5 calls per client_id per rolling minute, extras rejected): no file or disk I/O on the request path.
